title: Ethiopian Biology Entrance Exam 2016
description: Ethiopian Biology Entrance Exam 2016 - 100 multiple choice questions. Ethiopian national exam preparation material.

questions.questionText: Gene flow is the movement of genetic material
options: without altering the allele frequencies.
that drives a population towards perfection.
without affecting the balance of gene pool of a population.
where organisms either join or leave a population.
questions.explanation:
Gene flow, also known as gene migration, is the transfer of genetic material from one population to another.

 This occurs when organisms (or their gametes) either join or leave a population and reproduce, introducing new alleles or changing existing allele frequencies.

questions.questionText: Which one of the following options is a constituent of peripheral nervous system?
options: Afferent nerves, brain and automatic motor nerves
Somatic sensory nerves, spinal cord and efferent nerves
Afferent nerves, efferent nerves and somatic motor nerves
Spinal cord, afferent nerves and somatic sensory nerves
questions.explanation:
The Peripheral Nervous System (PNS) consists of all the nerves that lie outside the brain and spinal cord (which make up the Central Nervous System, CNS).

 These nerves are classified functionally into:
1. Afferent (Sensory) nerves that carry impulses to the CNS.

2. Efferent (Motor) nerves that carry impulses from the CNS. The Efferent division includes the Somatic Motor Nerves (voluntary control) and the Automatic Motor Nerves (involuntary control).

Therefore, Afferent nerves, efferent nerves and somatic motor nerves are all constituents of the PNS.

questions.questionText: Which one of the following structures of neurons is correctly paired with its function?
options: Axon - receives signal from muscle
Cell body - maintains structure and supply energy
Dendrites - protects the neuron and insulate it
Myelin sheath - reduces nerve impulse transmission
questions.explanation:
Let's review the functions:
Axon transmits the signal away from the cell body.
Cell body (Soma) contains the nucleus and cytoplasm, essential for maintaining structure and supplying energy (metabolic center).
Dendrites receives signals from other neurons or sensory receptors (like muscle). 
Myelin sheath speeds up (does not reduce) nerve impulse transmission by insulating the axon.  
Thus, the correct pairing is Cell body - maintains structure and supply energy.

questions.questionText: Which one of the following statements explain how nerve impulse is occurred? It occurs as a result of
options: charge difference across the membrane of axon.
The movement of neurotransmitter molecules into myelin sheath.
balanced charge across the membrane of dendrites.
The movement of neurotransmitter molecules out of cell body.
questions.explanation:
A nerve impulse, or action potential, is generated by a rapid, temporary change in the electrical potential across the axon membrane. 

This occurs due to the movement of ions (primarily Na+ and K+) across the membrane, creating A charge difference across the membrane of axon (depolarization and repolarization).

questions.questionText: Which one of the following statements is an acceptable justification of the importance of synapse? Synapse is
options: the mechanism of protecting the axon from external damage
connection between the appendages of consecutive neurons.
conductor of action potential towards the end of the dendrite.
the facilitator of the reverse flow of neurotransmitter chemical in neurons.
questions.explanation:
A synapse is the junction or gap between two neurons (a neuron and a target cell, like a muscle cell) where an impulse is transmitted.

 It represents the functional connection between the appendages of consecutive neurons (usually the axon terminal of one and the dendrite or cell body of the next). 

The signal transmission across this junction is primarily unidirectional and chemical (via neurotransmitters).

questions.questionText: Assume your friend has a blood type that has no antigen on his red blood cells but produces antibodies a and b, loses blood due to a car accident. If blood transfusion is necessary to save his life, your friend can receive blood from someone with
options: blood type AB.
blood type O.
blood type B.
blood type A.
questions.explanation:
The friend's blood has no antigens on the red blood cells but produces antibodies a and b.

 According to the ABO blood group system, this description corresponds to blood type O. Individuals with blood type O are universal donors but can only receive blood from other type O individuals, as receiving A, B, or AB blood would trigger a severe reaction from their anti-A and anti-B antibodies. 

Therefore, the friend can receive blood from someone with blood type O.

questions.questionText: The binomial system of naming developed by Linnaeus comprises two names. Which hierarchical groups are used?
options: Order and family
Genus and species
Kingdome and species
Kingdome and phylum
questions.explanation:
The binomial nomenclature system, introduced by Carolus Linnaeus, gives every organism a unique two-part scientific name. 

These two parts correspond to the taxonomic ranks of Genus (capitalized) and species (lowercase), always written in italics (e.g., Homo sapiens).

questions.questionText: Which one of the following is the feature of kingdom Monera? Its members are
options: unicellular without separated nucleus
multicellular with cell walls.
mainly autotrophic and saprophytic.
reproduced by hypha formation.
questions.explanation:
Kingdom Monera (now largely obsolete, replaced by Archaea and Bacteria) consists of Prokaryotes.
 Prokaryotic organisms are typically unicellular and lack a membrane-bound nucleus and other membrane-bound organelles. They are described as being without separated nucleus (meaning the genetic material, the nucleoid, is not enclosed by a membrane).

questions.questionText: Which alternative given below is comprised of harmful fungus from the kingdom Monera, Protista and Fungi, respectively?
options: Trypanosoma, Plasmodium falciparum and Haemophilus ducreyi
Candidaalbicans, Mycobacterium tuberculosis and Trypanosoma
Haemophilus ducreyi, Trypanosoma and Tinea pedis
Trypanosoma, Plasmodium falciparum and Penicillium
questions.explanation:
The question asks for a harmful member from Monera, Protista, and Fungi, in that specific order. Let's classify the correct option:

Haemophilus ducreyi is a bacterium (Kingdom Monera/Bacteria) that causes the STD chancroid.

Trypanosoma is a protozoan (Kingdom Protista) that causes diseases like sleeping sickness.
Tinea pedis (athlete's foot) is caused by a fungus (Kingdom Fungi).

Therefore, Haemophilus ducreyi, Trypanosoma and Tinea pedis is the correct sequence.

questions.questionText: Which one of the following is a feature of Octopi and squid in phylum mollusca? They have
options: segmented body with head and thorax.
well-developed brain.
lung as a breathing structure.
hard muscular foot with a hard body.
questions.explanation:
Octopi and squid are Cephalopods, the most highly evolved class of Molluscs.
 They are known for having the most complex nervous system among invertebrates, including a large, doughnut-shaped, well-developed brain enclosed in a cartilaginous cranium.

 They breathe using gills (not lungs), have a soft, unsegmented body, and their muscular foot is modified into arms/tentacles.

questions.questionText: What mechanism was used by Gregor Mendel to protect the garden peas from self-pollination? He
options: opened the flower bud before pollen matured.
sterilized the male part of the flower using chemicals.
covered the flower and protects it from pollinating agents.
selected pure dominant traits for breeding.
questions.explanation:
Mendel performed cross-pollination experiments on pea plants. 

To prevent the flowers from self-pollinating and to ensure he controlled which pollen fertilized which flower, he first castrated the flower (removed the stamens, the male parts) and then covered the flower and protects it from pollinating agents (like insects or wind) using bags or nets until he was ready to brush on pollen from a different parent plant.

questions.questionText: Gregor Mendel crossed two pure breeding traits of pea plants in his experiment and found only one of the traits expressed in the first generation. This shows that the
options: expressed trait must be determined by the recessive allele.
two traits in the F1 generation were equally expressed.
alleles masked in the F1 generation were lost due to mutation.
expressed trait must be determined by the dominant allele.
questions.explanation:
This observation is the basis of Mendel's Law of Dominance. When two pure-breeding parents (one dominant, one recessive) are crossed, only the dominant trait appears in the F1 generation, while the recessive trait is masked. 

The statement that the **expressed trait must be determined by the dominant allele** correctly explains this result.

questions.questionText: Which one of the following statements correctly describes chromosome structure?
options: pair of chromosomes is heteroygous in nature.
Chromosomes are similar to a gene in structure.
The DNA is wrapped with ribose sugar to form a chromosome.
Chromosomes are made up of histone bounded DNA.
questions.explanation:
A chromosome is the highest level of organization of genetic material. 
It is composed of a very long molecule of DNA that is tightly coiled and packaged around specialized proteins called histones.
 This complex of DNA and protein is called chromatin.

 Therefore, the statement that Chromosomes are made up of histone bounded DNA is the most accurate description of their composition.

questions.questionText: The breeding mechanism that improves the performance of animals or plants using particular traits is
options: self-breeding.
test cross.
selective breeding.
combination of traits.
questions.explanation:
Selective breeding (also called artificial selection) is the process by which humans choose organisms with desirable characteristics and intentionally breed them together over generations. 

The goal is to enhance specific, useful traits (like high yield in crops or fast running speed in animals) to improve the performance of animals or plants.

questions.questionText: Which one of the following birth control methods is correctly matched with its function?
options: Hormonal method - prevents follicle development and ovulation
Physical method - reduces the lining of the uterus
Surgical method - avoids carly embryo implantation
Natural method - prevent the ovum from reaching to the uterus
questions.explanation:
The correct match is Hormonal method - prevents follicle development and ovulation.

 Hormonal contraceptives (like the pill, patch, or ring) work primarily by introducing synthetic hormones that inhibit the release of FSH and LH, thereby preventing follicle development and ovulation (the release of an egg). Other methods have different primary functions:

 Physical methods (e.g., IUDs) mostly prevent implantation or fertilization.

 Surgical methods (e.g., vasectomy, tubal ligation) prevent the meeting of sperm and ovum.

 Natural methods (e.g., rhythm method) estimate the fertile window to avoid intercourse.

questions.questionText: The ability of carnivores to survive in an ecosystem is dependent on the availability of prey. This can be considered as
options: abiotic factor.
edaphe factor.
catastrophic factor.
biotic factor.
questions.explanation:
Ecosystem factors are broadly categorized as biotic (living components) or abiotic (non-living components). 

Since prey are living organisms that a carnivore eats, their availability is a D biotic factor that influences the survival and population size of the carnivore.

questions.questionText: This item is based on the following pyramid of biomass.
options: Grass, Cricket, Chicken and Lizard.
Grass, Cricket, Lizard and Chicken
Grass, Chicken, Cricket and Lizard
Grass, Lizard, Cricket and Chicken
questions.explanation: Review this question for further understanding.

questions.questionText: The two reverse processes that play a significant role in absorbing and releasing carbon dioxide, respectively are
options: combustion and photosynthesis.
decomposition and respiration.
respiration and assimilation.
photosynthesis and respiration.
questions.explanation: Photosynthesis absorbs carbon dioxide from the atmosphere to produce glucose, while respiration releases carbon dioxide as glucose is broken down to produce energy.

questions.questionText: Which one of the following adaptations is important for survival of polar bear in very cold environments? Having
options: smaller size
fine silky fur
blubbers under the skin
thick wrinkled cars
questions.explanation:
Polar bears rely on insulation to survive in the Arctic.
 Their most crucial adaptation for cold environments is a thick layer of fat called blubber under the skin.
 This layer provides excellent thermal insulation and also acts as an energy reserve. They also have dense fur, but the blubber is the primary thermal barrier.

questions.questionText: A student concluded that the stage of meiosis on a prepared slice of plant tissue he observed was Anaphase II. What do you think was the reason to come to this conclusion? Observation of
options: divided centromere and separated sister chromatids
reformed nuclear envelope and reappearance of nucleolus
one chromosome from each homologous pairs at the poles
crossing over between non-sister chromatids of homologous pairs
questions.explanation:
Anaphase II of meiosis is characterized by the physical separation of sister chromatids.
 This separation is immediately preceded by the division of the centromere that holds them together.
 The separated chromatids (now considered individual chromosomes) move toward opposite poles.

questions.questionText: Which one of the following plant species is endemic to Ethiopia?
options: Percica papaya
Eucalyptus globulose
Auracaria baramuleta
Guizotia abyssinica
questions.explanation:
An endemic species is native to and restricted to a specific region. 
Guizotia abyssinica is the scientific name for Noog or Niger Seed, which is known to be native to and most likely originated in the Ethiopian highlands, making it an endemic plant species of Ethiopia. 
Eucalyptus globulus is from Australia, and Carica papaya is from Central America.

questions.questionText: Which one of the following national parks of Ethiopia is declared as the world's heritage site and comprises endemic animals like Walia ibex?
options: Yangudi Rassa National Park
Simien Mountain National Park
Rift Valley National Park
Bale Mountain National Park
questions.explanation:
Simien Mountain National Park is a UNESCO World Heritage Site in Ethiopia.
 It is famous for its spectacular landscapes and is a vital habitat for several endemic species, most notably the critically endangered Walia ibex, a wild goat found nowhere else in the world.

questions.questionText: A mother milks her cow every morning and the milk usually forms curd after three days. What is the first step to investigate why this change happens?
options: Take action to prevent the milk from curdling
Read scientific articles about the reason for curdling of milk
Formulate hypothesis about the reason for milk curdling
Ask a question why the milk forms curd
questions.explanation:
The first step in a scientific investigation is to identify and ask a question about the observed phenomenon.
 In this case, the investigation begins by asking why the milk forms curd.

questions.questionText: A drug efficacy test was conducted under similar set up on two groups of infected mice (A and B). Group A were the control whereas group B were experimental group. A student gave a placebo to the control group and the drug to the experimental group. At the end, the experimental group got better. Which one of the following is true about the result?
options: Conclusion cannot be reached.
Placebo has better effect.
The drug has an effect.
The experiment was wrong.
questions.explanation: Since the control group received a placebo and did not improve while the experimental group received the drug and got better under the same conditions, the improvement can be attributed to the drug. Therefore, the drug has an effect.

questions.questionText: Suppose you did an experiment in a biology laboratory and need to report your work to your biology teacher. Which one of the following steps is correct to report the finding?
options: Title -> Procedure -> Result -> Hypothesis -> Prediction -> Evaluation
Title -> Hypothesis ->  Procedure -> Prediction -> Conclusion -> Result
Title -> Hypothesis -> Prediction -> Procedure -> Result -> Conclusion
Title -> Prediction -> Procedure -> Hypothesis -> Result -> Conclusion
questions.explanation: The correct order to report a scientific experiment is: start with the Title, state the Hypothesis, make a Prediction, describe the Procedure, present the Results, and end with the Conclusion.

questions.questionText: Which one of the following statements explains how the allosteric inhibitors act on enzymes? By binding to the
options: substrate and preventing it from binding to the active site
site other than the active site and altering the shape of the active site
active site of an enzyme and blocking the substrate
active site and altering the shape of the enzyme
questions.explanation:
Allosteric inhibitors bind to a site on the enzyme other than the active site (the allosteric site).
 This binding changes the shape of the enzyme, particularly the active site, preventing the substrate from binding effectively and thus reducing enzyme activity.

questions.questionText: Why are enzymes considered special molecules in metabolism? because
options: metabolic processes can produce special products in the presence of enzymes.
enzymes facilitate metabolic reactions under controlled physiological conditions.
enzymes are protein molecules that act as a source of energy.
reactions can't totally take place in the absence of enzymes.
questions.explanation: Enzymes are biological catalysts that speed up metabolic reactions without being consumed, allowing reactions to occur efficiently under normal physiological conditions of temperature and pH

questions.questionText: Which of the following is the most advanced and recent event in the history of cell biology?
options: Discovery of the double-helix structure of DNA
Enovation of the first scanning electron microscope
Description of the Golgi apparatus
Sequencing of the human genome
questions.explanation: The sequencing of the human genome, completed in the early 2000s, is the most recent and advanced milestone in cell biology compared to the discovery of DNA structure, the Golgi apparatus, or the invention of the scanning electron microscope.

questions.questionText: A student focused a slide of an onion epidermal cell on pre-estimated width of 2 millimeter field of view under a microscope. What will be the width of each individual cell if you count 8 cells that fit to the field of view during your observation?
options: 16 millimeter
0.25 millimeter
0.40 millimeter
4 millimeter
questions.explanation: The width of a single cell is calculated by dividing the field of view by the number of cells: 2 mm ÷ 8 = 0.25 mm

questions.questionText: Which one of the following statements is correct about the differences between eukaryotic and prokaryotic cells? Prokaryotic cells have
options: membrane bound organelles whereas eukaryotic cells don't have it.
small ribosomes whereas eukaryotic cells have large ribosomes.
cell wall whereas eukaryotic cells don't have cell wall.
division of labor whereas eukaryotic cells don't have it.
questions.explanation:
Prokaryotic cells have 70S ribosomes, which are smaller than the 80S ribosomes found in eukaryotic cells. 
Eukaryotic cells have membrane-bound organelles and more complex internal structures, unlike prokaryotes.

questions.questionText: Which biological tool is correctly matched with its function?
options: Petri dishes - to culture microorganisms
Burette - to measure mass of a substance
Centrifuges - to collect insects
Theodolite - to measure the rate of water flow
questions.explanation:
Petri dishes are shallow, flat-lidded dishes used to culture and grow microorganisms under controlled conditions.
 The other options are incorrectly matched with their functions.

questions.questionText: A student centrifuge a solution containing plant material in order to separate them based on their mass. After 10 minutes of centrifugation some of the components move to the bottom (A), others to the middle layer (B) and the remaining ones to the top layer (C). Which alternative shows the mass of the components in decreasing order?
options: C > A > B
B > A > C
A > B > C
A = B = C
questions.explanation: Review this question for further understanding.

questions.questionText: Which one of the following statements shows the future promise of biological sciences?
options: Finding alternative living place for human population
Using stem cells to repair damaged organs and grow new organ
Finding the adaptation mechanism of plant in new condition
Advising the government on how to conserve environment
questions.explanation: The use of stem cells to repair or replace damaged tissues and organs represents a cutting-edge and promising application of biological sciences in medicine, highlighting its future potential.

questions.questionText: Which one of the following alternatives contains only organic molecules?
options: Glucose, carbon dioxide, glycine and linoleic acid
Methane, calcium carbonate, linoleic acid and glucose
Methane, glycine, linoleic acid and glucose
Linoleic acid, glucose, calcium carbonate and methane
questions.explanation:
Organic molecules contain carbon-hydrogen (C-H) bonds.

 Methane (CH4), glycine (an amino acid), linoleic acid (a fatty acid), and glucose (a carbohydrate) are all organic molecules. Calcium carbonate (CaCO3) and carbon dioxide (CO2) are inorganic.

questions.questionText: Which one of the following properties permits insects to freely walk on water? Its high
options: specific heat capacity
latent heat of vaporization
adhesive force
surface tension
questions.explanation:
The ability of insects, such as water striders, to walk on water is due to the high surface tension of water.
 Surface tension is the cohesive force among water molecules at the surface that creates a film-like effect, resisting external force.

questions.questionText: Which one of the following properties of enzymes shows their catalytic nature?
options: Being non-specific to substrates
Reducing the activation energy
Being altered in a chemical reaction
Changing the nature of the product
questions.explanation: Enzymes are biological catalysts because they speed up chemical reactions by lowering the activation energy required for the reaction to occur, without being consumed or altered in the process.

questions.questionText: If an enzyme is named as "EC 3.4.11.1" in a systematic naming, what does the number " 3 " represents?
options: sub-subclass of an enzyme in relation to its protein nature.
ultra-subclass of an enzyme that is related to the place where they act.
sub-class of an enzyme in relation to the source from where it was discovered.
main class of an enzyme which indicates the type of reaction it catalyses.
questions.explanation:
In the Enzyme Commission (EC) numbering system, the first number represents the main class of the enzyme, indicating the type of chemical reaction it catalyzes.

 For example, '3' denotes hydrolases, which catalyze hydrolysis reactions.

questions.questionText: In the lock-and-key model of enzymatic action, the activation energy is lowered through
options: provision of alternative pathway for the reaction.
straining of the substrate molecules bound to the active site.
conformational change of substrate molecules.
permanent modification of the active site of the enzyme.
questions.explanation:
In the lock-and-key model, the substrate fits precisely into the enzyme's active site.

 Binding strains certain chemical bonds in the substrate, making it easier for the reaction to occur and thereby lowering the activation energy.

questions.questionText: Which one of the following minerals are used as cofactor for the enzymed alcohol dehydrogenase?
options: Cobalions
Ferrous ions
Magnesium ions
Zinc ions
questions.explanation:
Alcohol dehydrogenase requires zinc ions (Zn²⁺) as a cofactor. 
Zinc helps stabilize the enzyme structure and plays a key role in the catalytic activity during the oxidation of alcohols.

questions.questionText:
A student made an experiment to observe the effect of Temperature on catalase of mashed potato. After three parallel trials, he obtained the following results.
At which temperature was the reaction fastest?
questions.explanation: Review this question for further understanding.

questions.questionText: Which one of the following organic molecules observes ester bonds in its molecular structure?
options: Triglyceride
Amino acid
Glycogen
Cellulose
questions.explanation:
Triglycerides are fats composed of one glycerol molecule bonded to three fatty acids through ester bonds.
 Amino acids, glycogen, and cellulose do not contain ester bonds in their basic structures.

questions.questionText: Which one of the following statement is correct about the structural organization of hemoglobin? It is formed
options: when a polypeptide chain folds itself during protein synthesis.
through the association of two or more polypeptide chains.
through folding of secondary structure of a polypeptide chain.
by hydrogen bonding between quaternary and tertiary structures.
questions.explanation: Hemoglobin is a quaternary protein made of four polypeptide chains (two alpha and two beta chains) that associate together to form a functional protein capable of carrying oxygen.

questions.questionText: The presence of large amount of lipid reduces the density of an animal. Which function of triglycerides is related to this fact?
options: Thermal insulation
Waterproofing
Buoyancy
Respiratory substrate
questions.explanation: Triglycerides are less dense than water, so storing large amounts of lipids helps animals, especially aquatic ones, maintain buoyancy and float more easily.

questions.questionText: The missing number represented by the letter " n " in the formula of maltose (C12H18O11) is
questions.explanation: Review this question for further understanding.

questions.questionText: According to biological scenario, structure is related to function, which one of the following is correctly described?
options: Trachea - millions of air sacs for diffusion of O2 and CO2
Alveoli - supported by cartilage for swallowing foods
Nasal passage - large surface area with hairs for filtration of air
Larynx - hair like strictures for mucus production
questions.explanation: The nasal passage has hairs (vibrissae) and a large surface area to filter, warm, and humidify the air before it enters the lungs. Other options incorrectly match structures with functions.

questions.questionText: As compared to the exhaled air, the inhaled air contains
options: 70% oxygen, 0.03% carbon dioxide and 30% nitrogen.
16% oxygen, 4% carbon dioxide and 80% nitrogen.
80% oxygen, 20% carbon dioxide and 0.04% nitrogen.
21% oxygen, 0.04% carbon dioxide and 80% nitrogen.
questions.explanation:
Inhaled air contains approximately 21% oxygen, 0.04% carbon dioxide, and the majority as nitrogen (~78–80%).
 The composition changes in exhaled air due to gas exchange in the lungs

questions.questionText:
A student conducted a food test on three unknown food samples and obtained results as presented in the table below.

What do you conclude from the result of the above experiment?
options: Lipids and reducing sugars are absent from all the three food samples tested.
Proteins and reducing sugars are found in all the food samples at equal concentrations.
Non - reducing sugars are present in all the food samples at different concentrations.
Reducing sugars are found in two of the samples and proteins are found in all the samples.
questions.explanation: Review this question for further understanding.

questions.questionText: What is the scientific reason behind the preference of high altitude areas for training by the Ethiopian Athletes? Because
options: the RBCs produced are more efficient than those at low altitude.
it helps them to adapt to the high atmospheric pressure of mountains.
the oxygen density is higher than the low altitude.
it helps them to increase their lung capacities.
questions.explanation:
Training at high altitudes exposes athletes to lower oxygen levels, stimulating the production of more red blood cells (RBCs) and hemoglobin.

 These RBCs improve oxygen transport efficiency, enhancing endurance when the athlete returns to lower altitudes.

questions.questionText: How does oxygen is transported in the human body? It is transported
options: by simple diffusion along concentration gradient from the lungs to the heart.
from the red blood cells to actively respiring tissues by facilitated
from the lungs to actively respiring tissue by hemoglobin of RBC .
by the blood plasma from lower concentration to higher concentration.
questions.explanation: Oxygen is carried in the blood primarily by hemoglobin in red blood cells. Hemoglobin binds oxygen in the lungs and transports it to tissues where it is released for cellular respiration

questions.questionText: Which one of the following statements is well justified, why the left ventricle is tough in nature? because it
options: forces oxygenated blood out of the heart.
returns deoxygenated blood to the heart.
returns oxygenated blood to the heart.
forces deoxygenated blood out of the heart.
questions.explanation: The left ventricle has thick, muscular walls because it must generate high pressure to force oxygenated blood through the aorta and the entire systemic circulation.

questions.questionText: Which one of the following statements is true about female genital mutilation?
options: gives acceptance for marriage.
helps to deliver baby easily.
imposes risk of infection.
keeps girls pure and honest.
questions.explanation:
Female genital mutilation (FGM) is a harmful cultural practice that can cause severe health risks, including infections, bleeding, and long-term complications.

 The other options reflect cultural myths, not biological or medical facts.

questions.questionText: Assume that you have a friend who is HIV positive and you are familiar about the case. How can you support your friend if she is injured and needs your help?
options: Help your friend with precautions
Ignore your friend because of the virus
Call to other people to protect you from the virus
Help your friend without any fear of the virus
questions.explanation: HIV cannot be transmitted through casual contact. When assisting an HIV-positive person who is injured, you should help them while taking standard precautions (like using gloves for open wounds) to prevent any risk of infection from blood or body fluids.

questions.questionText: Why are root hairs efficient in uptake of water from the soil? Because they
options: anchor the plant to the ground.
show positive hydrotropism.
keep turgidity of the cell.
have high surface area to volume ratio.
questions.explanation: Root hairs increase the surface area of roots, allowing more water and mineral ions to be absorbed efficiently from the soil.

questions.questionText: what will happen to a plant if the apical dominance is removed through repeated pruning? The
options: plant shades its leaves to withstand the condition.
plant elongates and bends to one direction.
side shoots grow quickly and the plant becomes bushy.
growth of the lateral shoots will be inhibited.
questions.explanation:
Apical dominance occurs when the main shoot apex inhibits the growth of lateral buds through the action of auxins.

 Removing the apical bud by pruning reduces auxin levels, allowing lateral buds to grow faster, making the plant bushy.

questions.questionText: A farmer sowed cotton seeds in a farm land which fulfills the optimum conditions for germination. After a few days, he observed the newly growing seedlings. Which of the following statements is correct about the farmer's observation?
options: growth of plumule above the soil surface
remaining of the cotyledon below the ground
hypogeal germination of the hypocotyl
growth of plumule without forming a hook
questions.explanation: In cotton (a dicot plant), germination is epigeal, meaning the cotyledons are pushed above the soil as the hypocotyl elongates, forming a hook to protect the plumule, which eventually grows above the soil surface.

questions.questionText: Which one of the following is the main function of Bowman's capsule of the human kidneys?
options: Mineral reabsorption
Prevent back flow of urine
Ultrafiltration of blood
Water preservation
questions.explanation: Bowman's capsule surrounds the glomerulus and performs ultrafiltration, filtering blood plasma (including water, ions, and small molecules) into the nephron while retaining blood cells and large proteins in the blood.

questions.questionText: What is the justification for feeling warm while sweating a lot in a very humid condition?
options: the lower rate of evaporation of water from the skin surfaces
Closure of the glands in the epidermal layer of the skin
An increase in metabolic rate as temperature increases
Unequal distribution of ions on membrane of cells
questions.explanation:
In high humidity, the air is already saturated with moisture, so sweat does not evaporate efficiently from the skin.
 Evaporation is necessary for cooling, so the body feels warm despite sweating.

questions.questionText: As a result of human activities, huge amount of carbon dioxide has been accumulated in the atmosphere. What is the consequence of this phenomenon?
options: Drop in temperature of the earth and death of aquatic organisms
Increased rate of uptake of carbon dioxide by green plants
Preventing certain amount of heat escaping back to the space
Reduction in the sea level and death of aquatic animals
questions.explanation:
Excess carbon dioxide in the atmosphere traps heat, preventing it from escaping into space.
 This greenhouse effect leads to global warming and climate change.

questions.questionText: Among the following statements, one briefly describes the concept of climate change. It is the
options: Sudden change in an average rain fall of a limited area.
radical change of local weather condition that sustain for less than a year.
gradual change of atmospheric temperature over a short period of time.
global change in the temperature, precipitation and wind conditions.
questions.explanation: Climate change refers to long-term, global alterations in temperature, precipitation patterns, and wind conditions, affecting ecosystems and human societies worldwide.

questions.questionText: What was the main objective of the United Nations Framework Convention on Climate Change (UNFCCC)?
options: Reduction of the monopole utilization of border crossing rivers to prevent climate change
Prevention of dangerous man - made interference with the climate system
Donation of high carbon projects related to climate change by the developed countries
Prohibition of developing countries from setting up big industries that could affect the climate
questions.explanation: The main objective of the UNFCCC is to stabilize greenhouse gas concentrations in the atmosphere at a level that would prevent dangerous human-induced interference with the climate system.

questions.questionText: Which one of the following research activities has been conducted at Armauer Hansen Research Institute?
options: Improving crop production through genetic engineering
Conserving the genes of endemic plants and animals
Assessing the nutritional status of mothers and babies
Developing drugs for leshmaniasis and tuberculosis
questions.explanation: The Armauer Hansen Research Institute conducts biomedical research on infectious diseases, including tuberculosis and other tropical diseases like leishmaniasis, and contributes to the development of medical tools, treatments, and innovations in these areas.

questions.questionText: Which one of the following alternatives contains only protein rich cereals?
options: Red kidney peas, maize and white pea
White kidney peas, red kidney peas and chickpea
Barley, chickpea and groundnut
Wheat, red kidney peas and sesame
questions.explanation: White kidney peas, red kidney peas, and chickpeas are legumes, which are rich in protein. Cereals like wheat, maize, and barley contain some protein but are not as protein-dense as legumes.

questions.questionText: Which one of the following statements is correct about the process of digestion in the stomach?
options: Pepsin hydrolyzes protein molecules into amino acids.
Lipase hydrolyzes fat molecules into fatty acids and glycerol.
Amylase hydrolyzes starch molecules into maltose.
Bile hydrolyzes bigger fat molecules into smaller droplets.
questions.explanation: In the stomach, gastric lipase begins the digestion of fats by breaking down triglycerides into fatty acids and glycerol. Pepsin partially hydrolyzes proteins into peptides, not directly into amino acids. Amylase acts on starch in the mouth, and bile emulsifies fats but does not hydrolyze them

questions.questionText: Which one of the following statements is correct about the role of trypsin in digestion?
options: It acts on lipids in the small intestine.
It acts on maltose in the mouth.
It acts on starch in the stomach.
It acts on protein in the small intestine.
questions.explanation: Trypsin is a protease enzyme produced by the pancreas and secreted into the small intestine, where it hydrolyzes proteins into smaller peptides for further digestion

questions.questionText: Which one of the following descriptions about absorption of nutrients in the digestive system is correct?
options: Glycerol molecules are first absorbed into the hepatic portal vein and then to lacteal.
Amino acid molecules are directly absorbed from small intestine into the blood.
Glucose molecules are first absorbed into the lacteal and then enter into the blood.
Fatty acids molecules are absorbed from small intestine directly into the blood.
questions.explanation: Amino acids, as the products of protein digestion, are absorbed directly into the blood capillaries of the small intestine and transported via the hepatic portal vein to the liver. In contrast, fatty acids and glycerol are absorbed into lacteals (lymphatic vessels) before entering the bloodstream.

questions.questionText: What is the main function of the dermis of the skin?
options: Production of skin pigments
Prevention of the entry of pathogens
Synthesis of hair and nail proteins
Temperature regulation in homeostasis
questions.explanation: The dermis contains blood vessels, sweat glands, and sensory receptors that help regulate body temperature through vasodilation, vasoconstriction, and sweating, maintaining homeostasis. Production of pigments occurs in the epidermis, not the dermis.

questions.questionText:
This Item is based on the following diagram about eye structure.

The part of the eye represented by letter **" Y "** is
options: ciliary muscle.
optic nerve.
iris.
pupil.
questions.explanation: Review this question for further understanding.

questions.questionText: A man observed elementary school students spinning around, and realized that none of them could properly walk upright after sudden interruption of the spinning. Which one of the following is the correct reason for this condition?
options: The fluid in the semi secular canal stopped immediately when the body stopped spinning.
The sensory cells were unable to detect stimulus after the spinning was quitted.
The fluid in the semicircular canal kept moving after the spinning was stopped.
The nerve impulse was transmitted after the spinning was stopped.
questions.explanation:
In the inner ear, the semicircular canals contain endolymph fluid that continues to move due to inertia when spinning stops suddenly. 
This ongoing movement bends hair cells, sending signals to the brain that cause dizziness and temporary loss of balance.

questions.questionText: Which of the following is the correct description of hormones? They are chemical messengers that
options: transmit message faster than the nerve system.
regulates many physiological process.
targets only the site of secretion.
are produced in glands that contain ducts.
questions.explanation: Hormones are chemical messengers secreted by endocrine glands into the bloodstream. They regulate a wide range of physiological processes in target organs or tissues, even at sites far from where they are produced.

questions.questionText: Homeostasis is a mechanism of
options: keeping internal body environment constant.
adjusting the environment relative to body condition.
keeping external environment stable.
protecting the body from pathogens.
questions.explanation: Homeostasis is the biological process that maintains a stable internal environment (such as temperature, pH, and water balance) despite changes in the external environment.

questions.questionText: Which one of the following arrangement of molecules in the fluid mosaic model of the cell membrane is correct?
options: Phospholipids fill the protein like a sandwich to retain its rigidity.
Phospholipid molecules are peripherally attached to proteins.
Phospholipids are inserted into the bilayer of protein molecules.
Protein molecules are studded between the phospholipid bilayers.
questions.explanation: In the fluid mosaic model, the cell membrane consists of a phospholipid bilayer with proteins embedded (integral proteins) or attached (peripheral proteins). This arrangement allows fluidity and selective transport across the membrane.

questions.questionText: What is the role of cholesterol in the cell membrane? It
options: anchors integral proteins to the cytoskeleton.
reduce the fluidity of the cell membrane.
acts as receptor site for hormones and other signaling molecules.
transports hydrophilic molecules into the cell.
questions.explanation:
Cholesterol molecules are interspersed within the phospholipid bilayer of the cell membrane. 

They stabilize the membrane structure by reducing fluidity at high temperatures and preventing it from becoming too rigid at low temperatures.

questions.questionText:
This item is based on the following table on the function of cellular organelles:

Which numbers in the above table show the correct function of the given organelles?
options: 2 and 4
2 and 3
1 and 4
1 and 3
questions.explanation: Review this question for further understanding.

questions.questionText: Potato slices of equal weighed were immersed in four different concentrations of salt solutions. The solutions were **1.5, 1.0, 0.5, and 0.1 molars**. After a day, the potato slices were re-weighted. Which potato slice weighs the least? The one from
options: 0.1 molars
1.5 molars
0.5 molars
1.0 molars
questions.explanation: Review this question for further understanding.

questions.questionText: Suppose you took a container and divided it into two halves by a membrane which is permeable to water and labelled the two halves " A " and " B ". Finally you added hypertonic solution in " A " and hypotonic solution in " B ". What will be the expected result of this experiment? The water level of
options: " A " remains constant.
both " A " and " B " rise up.
" B " decreases.
" B " rises up.
questions.explanation: Review this question for further understanding.

questions.questionText: During oxidative phosphorylation, ATP is produced by combining ADP and inorganic phosphate using energy released from
options: transport of electrons from complex IV to complex I.
dehydrogenation of pyruvate to acetyl CoA.
decarboxylation of citrate to oxaloacetate.
transfer of electrons from NADH/FADH₂ to O₂.
questions.explanation: During oxidative phosphorylation, electrons from NADH and FADH₂ are transferred through the electron transport chain to oxygen, releasing energy. This energy drives ATP synthase to combine ADP and inorganic phosphate to form ATP.

questions.questionText: In a fox population, foxes with thicker fur survived better in cold climate compared to those with thinner fur. However, foxes with thinner fur survived better when the climate was very hot. What type of natural selection is described in this scenario?
options: Diversifying selection
Extreme selection
Stabilizing selection
Directional selection
questions.explanation:
Diversifying (or disruptive) selection favors individuals at both extremes of a trait while selecting against intermediate forms.

 In this case, foxes with either very thick or very thin fur have higher survival depending on the climate, while intermediate fur thickness is less advantageous.

questions.questionText: Which one of the following comparisons between substrate level and oxidative phosphorylation is correct?
options: 34 ATP molecules are produced, but in oxidative phosphorylation 4 ATP molecules are produced per glucose molecule.
ATP is made in the cytosol and matrix, but in oxidative phosphorylation it is made on the inner membrane of mitochondria.
protons are pumped into the inter-membrane space, but in oxidative phosphorylation they are pumped into the cytosol.
oxygen is the final electron acceptor, but in oxidative phosphorylation NAD is the electron acceptor.
questions.explanation:
Substrate-level phosphorylation occurs in the cytosol (glycolysis) and mitochondrial matrix (Krebs cycle), directly forming ATP from ADP.

 Oxidative phosphorylation occurs on the inner mitochondrial membrane, using energy from the electron transport chain to produce ATP.

questions.questionText: Which one of the following determines the cause and effect of lactate production during physical exercise? The demand for
options: substrate that can easily release energy leads to production of lactate which results in muscle fatigue.
an easily absorbable molecule leads to the production of lactate that results in muscle fatigue.
lower pH in muscle tissues leads to fermentation of respiratory substrates leading to muscle fatigue.
more energy causes muscle cells to ferment respiratory substrates leading to muscle fatigue.
questions.explanation:
During intense exercise, oxygen supply to muscle cells may be insufficient for aerobic respiration.

 To meet the high energy demand, muscles perform anaerobic respiration (fermentation), producing lactate. Accumulation of lactate lowers pH and contributes to muscle fatigue.

questions.questionText: The view of biochemical origin of life hypothesized that the first life forms appeared in warm, primitive ocean and were heterotrophic. Which one of the following statements can support this idea?
options: Life is the inherent property of the universe which permits unlimited existence
The appearance of dust of unknown source with microbial spores that can feed on organic molecules.
The formation of abundant organic molecules due to radiations and the absence of oxygen led to the primitive living organisms.
Resistant spores from meteorites reached to the earth and used organic molecules to survive in the environment.
questions.explanation:
The biochemical (primordial soup) hypothesis suggests that in the oxygen-free early oceans, energy from radiation, lightning, or UV light enabled the formation of organic molecules.

 These molecules accumulated and were used by heterotrophic primitive life forms.

questions.questionText: Which statement shows the correct comparison between the Lamarck's and Darwin's theory of evolution?
options: Lamarck believed in the development of new traits due to variation while Darwin believed in their occurrence due to use and disuse of organs.
Darwin recognized the origin of species was through mutation while Lamarck believed it was through effect of the environment.
Lamarck believed the gradual occurrence of changes while Darwin believed in the immediate change of species.
Darwin claimed that variation is heritable while Lamarck considers variation as acquired traits.
questions.explanation:
Darwin's theory of natural selection relies on heritable variations in populations that confer survival advantages.

 Lamarck proposed that traits acquired during an organism's lifetime (e.g., through use or disuse) could be passed to offspring, which is now known to be incorrect.

questions.questionText: Which of the following is true concerning the evidences of evolution?
options: Organisms which have little genetic relationship show similar behavior.
Organisms which live in the same area have similar evolutionary history.
Species that are closely related share the most similar DNA sequence.
Species that live in the same geographic area have the same genetic makeup.
questions.explanation:
Genetic evidence of evolution shows that species with close evolutionary relationships have highly similar DNA sequences, reflecting their shared ancestry. 

Geographic proximity or behavior alone does not necessarily indicate close genetic relationship.

questions.questionText: In Human evolution brain size increased over the courses of evolution: Which alternative contains hominids arranged in an increasing order of brain size?
options: Homo neandertalensis --> Homo erecus --> Homo habilis --> Homo
Homo erceras --> Homo habilis --> Homo neandertalensis --> Homo sapiens
Homo erectus --> Homo Acandertalensis --> Homo habilis --> Homo
Homo habilis --> Homo erectus --> Homo neandertalensis --> Homo sapiens
questions.explanation: Review this question for further understanding.

questions.questionText: The type of gene mutation that results in the change of a triplet (GAG) in a normal hemoglobin to another triplet (GTG) in sickle-cell hemoglobin is
options: deletion mutation.
substitution.
insertion mutation.
non-disjunction.
questions.explanation:
Sickle-cell anemia is caused by a point mutation in the β-globin gene where a single nucleotide is substituted: the codon GAG (glutamic acid) is replaced by GTG (valine).

 This is a classic example of a substitution mutation.

questions.questionText: Which one of the following statements correctly explains the genetic drift? It is a change in allele frequency due to
options: an independent assortment of chromosomes.
non- random mating of individuals in a population.
chance based sampling error.
relocation of species into other areas.
questions.explanation:
Genetic drift refers to random changes in allele frequencies in a population due to chance events, especially in small populations.

 It is not driven by natural selection, mating patterns, or migration.

questions.questionText: Identify the correct mechanism of bacterial reproduction by conjugation.
options: Mitotic spindles are produced to separate bacterial DNA into two equal parts.
The recipient bacteria use their pili to pull the donor bacteria during plasmid transfer.
Bacteria take up genetic materials of dead organisms and integrate into their DNA.
pair of bacteria come together and exchanges their plasmids.
questions.explanation:
In bacterial conjugation, two bacterial cells connect through a conjugation pilus.
 The donor transfers plasmid DNA to the recipient, resulting in genetic exchange between the two bacteria.

questions.questionText: Which one of the following features is NOT the characteristic feature of fungi? They
options: have haploid nuclei and multinucleate hypha.
reproduce asexually through spore production.
are either autotrophic, parasitic or saprophytic.
exhibit apical growth of networked hypha.
questions.explanation:
Fungi are heterotrophic organisms; they cannot make their own food (not autotrophic).

 They obtain nutrients by absorption and are commonly parasitic or saprophytic. They typically have haploid nuclei, multinucleate hyphae, reproduce by spores, and show apical growth of hyphae.

questions.questionText: What is the argument behind the need of appropriate host cell for viruses to replicate themselves? Because viruses
options: are obligate saprophyte that can only replicate inside a cell.
have cell surface antigen specific to a given cell type.
lack metabolic capacity to produce energy outside cells.
lack of double strand DNA to duplicate themselves.
questions.explanation:
Viruses are obligate intracellular parasites because they lack the metabolic machinery and energy-producing systems (such as ribosomes and enzymes for ATP production) required for independent replication.

 Therefore, they must infect a suitable host cell to reproduce.

questions.questionText: Which one of the following diseases and their mode of transmission is correctly matched?
options: Salmoneliosis - contaminated food
Candidiasis - droplet infection
Chicken pox - fecal-oral route
Common cold - direct contact
questions.explanation:
Salmoneliosis is typically transmitted through consumption of contaminated food or water.
 Candidiasis is usually caused by overgrowth of normal flora, chicken pox spreads mainly through airborne droplets, and the common cold is primarily transmitted through droplets and contact with contaminated surfaces.

questions.questionText: What is the basic difference between anabolism and catabolism?
options: Anabolism is related to respiration while catabolism is to photosynthesis.
Catabolism is condensation while anabolism is hydrolysis reaction.
Anabolism is energy absorbing while catabolism is energy releasing process.
Catabolism is a constructive while anabolism is destructive reaction.
questions.explanation:
Anabolism involves building complex molecules from simpler ones and requires an input of energy (endergonic process).
 Catabolism involves breaking down complex molecules into simpler ones and releases energy (exergonic process).

questions.questionText: A transgenic organism is an organism that
options: replicates its DNA without control.
can undergo chromosomal non-disjunction.
has received genetic material of another organism.
is artificially cultured and harvested.
questions.explanation:
A transgenic organism is one that has been genetically modified by introducing a gene (foreign DNA) from another species using biotechnology techniques.

 This inserted gene allows the organism to express new traits.

questions.questionText: Which of the following explains how biology takes part in biosensor technology? Using microorganism to
options: monitor pollutants
extract metals from ores
develop vaccines
produce antibiotics
questions.explanation:
In biosensor technology, microorganisms or biological components (such as enzymes or antibodies) are used to detect and monitor specific substances, including environmental pollutants. 
The biological response is converted into a measurable signal.

questions.questionText: In a textile industry microorganism's commercial products play significant role in removing stains like grease by changing
options: the acidic or basic nature of the stain molecules.
the temperature of insoluble large stain molecules.
the color of stain molecules to another color.
large insoluble stain molecules into small and soluble ones.
questions.explanation: Microorganisms produce enzymes such as lipases and proteases that break down large, insoluble stain molecules (like grease and proteins) into smaller, soluble molecules. This makes the stains easier to wash away in textile processing.

questions.questionText: Which one of the following statements is correct about application of biopesticide in agriculture? It
options: uses bacteria and fungi or their metabolites to kill insects.
breakdowns glyphosate by an enzyme introduced into plant cell culture.
produces insect resistant crops through modification of the plant genes using bacterial plasmids.
produces toxic chemicals by crops through modification of their genes.
questions.explanation:
Biopesticides involve the use of natural organisms such as bacteria, fungi, or their metabolic products to control agricultural pests.
 For example, Bacillus thuringiensis (Bt) produces toxins that specifically kill certain insect larvae.

questions.questionText: Which one of the following statements correctly describes bacteria? They are
options: multicellular eukaryotic organisms.
single celled prokaryotic organisms.
single celled eukaryotic organisms.
multicellular prokaryotic organisms.
questions.explanation:
Bacteria are unicellular (single-celled) organisms that lack a true nucleus and membrane-bound organelles.
 Therefore, they are classified as prokaryotes.

questions.questionText: Which one among the following processes occurs during the light independent phase of photosynthesis?
options: Cyclic photophosphorylation of ADP in the thylakoid
Excitation of electrons from chlorophyll molecules
Splitting of water molecules into its components
Reduction of triose molecules by hydrogen from NADPH
questions.explanation: During the light-independent phase (Calvin cycle) of photosynthesis, ATP and NADPH produced in the light-dependent reactions are used to reduce 3-carbon molecules (triose phosphates) to form glucose and other carbohydrates.

questions.questionText: As compared to non- cyclic photophosphorylation, the cyclic photophosphorylation uses the
options: photosystem I as the last electron acceptor.
photosystem I to produce ATP and reduced NADP in the stroma.
hydrolysis of water to replace electrons lost from photosystem II.
photosystem II as the first electron donor to NADP.
questions.explanation:
In cyclic photophosphorylation, electrons excited in Photosystem I are cycled back to the same photosystem via the electron transport chain, producing ATP but not NADPH. 

There is no involvement of Photosystem II or water splitting in this process.

questions.questionText: Which one of the following chemical reactions summarizes the process of photosynthesis?
options: C₆H₁₂O₆ + 6O₂ --> 6CO₂ + 6H₂O + 12H₂O
6CO₂ + 6H₂O --> C₆H₁₂O₆ + 6O₂ + ATP
C₆H₁₂O₆ + 6O₂ --> 6CO₂ + 6H₂O + ATP
6CO₂ + 12H₂O --> C₆H₁₂O₆ + 6O₂ + 6H₂O
questions.explanation:
Photosynthesis uses carbon dioxide and water in the presence of light energy to produce glucose and oxygen.

 The overall balanced reaction is: 6CO₂ + 12H₂O → C₆H₁₂O₆ + 6O₂ + 6H₂O.

questions.questionText: Which one of the following statements properly describes the structure of ATP? It is made up of
options: one adenine base attached to a pentose sugar and three phosphate groups.
two adenine bases attached to a hexose sugar and three phosphate groups.
two adenine bases attached to a deoxyribose sugar and two phosphate groups.
one adenine base attached to a ribose sugar and two phosphate groups.
questions.explanation:
ATP (adenosine triphosphate) consists of a single adenine base attached to a five-carbon sugar (ribose) and three phosphate groups. 
It serves as the primary energy carrier in cells.

questions.questionText: Which one of the following descriptions about glycolysis is correct? It is a process
options: of producing acetyl CoA from pyruvate by releasing CO2.
that produces a net of 4 ATP through substrate level phosphorylation.
of breaking down of a glucose molecule to two pyruvates.
that takes place in the cytosol with high demand of oxygen.
questions.explanation:
Glycolysis is the metabolic pathway in which one glucose molecule (C₆H₁₂O₆) is broken down into two molecules of pyruvate.

 It occurs in the cytosol, does not require oxygen (anaerobic), and produces a net of 2 ATP molecules per glucose.
